{{short description|None}}

{{Infobox Olympic sport
|image = [[File:ski jumping pictogram.svg|150px|class=skin-invert]]
|code = SJP
|sport = ski jumping
|menevents = 3
|womenevents = 2
|mixedevents=1}}
[[Ski jumping]] has been included in the program of every [[Winter Olympic Games]]. From [[1924 Winter Olympics|1924]] through to [[1956 Winter Olympics|1956]], the competition involved jumping from one hill whose length varied from each edition of the Games to the next.

It is disputed whether the Olympic ski jumping events from 1924 to [[1960 Winter Olympics|1960]] were normal hill or large hill competitions. Even the [[International Olympic Committee]] (IOC) has no clear consensus on this question.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/chamonix-1924/results/ski-jumping/normal-hill-individual-men |title=Chamonix 1924 Normal Hill Individual Men Results - Olympic Ski Jumping |website=olympics.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/olympic-games/squaw-valley-1960/results/ski-jumping/normal-hill-individual-men |title=Squaw Valley 1960 Normal Hill Individual Men Results - Olympic Ski Jumping |website=olympics.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.olympics.com/en/sports/ski-jumping/ |title=Olympic Ski Jumping |website=olympics.com}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Olympedia – Ski Jumping |url=https://www.olympedia.org/sports/SJP |website=[[Olympedia]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Ski Jumping &#124; Milano Cortina 2026 | url=https://milanocortina2026.olympics.com/en/ski-jumping }}</ref>

Most historians have placed the length of the Olympic [[ski jump]] hill in 1924 at 70&nbsp;meters and have classified this as the ''large hill''.<ref>{{cite web |title=Olympedia – Large Hill, Individual, Men |url=https://www.olympedia.org/results/2350 |website=[[Olympedia]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Winter Olympics: Ski Jumping | url=https://www.infoplease.com/winter-olympics-ski-jumping }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Large hill M - Ski Jumping at the 1924 Winter Olympics in Chamonix - Results | url=https://www.olympiandatabase.com/index.php?id=12261&L=1 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Olympic Ski Jumping History: Champions, Records, Evolution and Iconic Moments &#124; NBC Olympics | url=https://www.nbcolympics.com/news/ski-jumping-101-olympic-history }}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=The first large hill of Germany | url=https://www.skisprungschanzen.com/EN/Articles/0035-The+first+large+hill+of+Germany+ }}</ref> (Recent information from the [[International Ski Federation|FIS]] offices in [[Switzerland]] have had the K-points from 1924 to 1956 determined as shown below). In 1960, the ski jump hill was standardized to 80&nbsp;meters. In 1964, a second ski jump, the ''normal hill'' at 70&nbsp;meters (K90) was added along with the 80&nbsp;meters (K120) ''large hill''. The length of the large hill run in 1968 increased from 80&nbsp;meters to 90&nbsp;meters (K120). The team large hill event was added in 1988. By 1992, the ski jumping competitions were referred to by their K-point distances rather than their run length prior to launching from the ski jump (90&nbsp;meters for the normal hill and 120&nbsp;meters for the large hill, respectively) and have been that way ever since. For the [[2006 Winter Olympics]], the normal hill was designated as HS106 (K95) while the large hill was designated as HS140 (K125).

Until [[1980 Winter Olympics|1980]], the Winter Olympics also served as the [[FIS Nordic World Ski Championships]] for ski jumping in Olympic years. During this period, the Olympic medalists received an additional medal from FIS. 

On April 6, 2011, the IOC officially accepted women's ski jumping into the official Olympic program for the [[2014 Winter Olympics]] in Sochi, Russia. On February 11, 2014, [[Carina Vogt]] of Germany won the first gold medal for women's ski jumping at the Winter Olympic Games.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/winter-olympics/26057176|title=Sochi 2014: Carina Vogt wins women's ski jumping gold |date=11 February 2014 |work=BBC Sport |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221014072536/https://www.bbc.com/sport/winter-olympics/26057176 |archive-date=14 October 2022 |last=Hodgetts |first=Rob}}</ref>
